faq.q: What is an AI spokesperson video?
faq.a: A short ad where a generated presenter holds your product and says a line. You choose the look, the voice, and the language. They are not a cartoon and not a customer. You start from your photo or a product link.

faq.q: How does a spokesperson video get made?
faq.a: Paste your line, or let a script be written from the product page. Pick a presenter and a voice. Captions and a song from the music library can be added in the built-in editor. Your own shop software can also ask for a clip through an API, a connection made for other tools.

faq.q: Where can I use an AI spokesperson?
faq.a: On paid ads, product pages, social feeds, and short guides. The same presenter can explain one feature, a setup step, or an offer.

faq.q: Can a spokesperson explain the product?
faq.a: Yes. Each new clip can say the same point, so the feature you care about is the one shoppers hear.

faq.q: Can a spokesperson walk through setup?
faq.a: Yes. Use it for setup, sizing, or daily use. When the product changes, update the line and make the clip again, including in another language.

faq.q: How do shops use a spokesperson on social?
faq.a: They write several opening lines from one photo, and keep one presenter as the face of the product. A group of clips can cover more than one item.

faq.q: Can I choose the look, the voice, or the language?
faq.a: Yes. The actor library has presenters for different settings. Pick an AI voice and a language that matches the buyer. Review the clip before you post.

faq.q: Can I run the clip as an ad?
faq.a: Yes. You can use finished clips for your shop, and they have no watermark. Plans start at $24.50 a month. A 10-second clip uses 40 credits. Credits are what each video spends. If the video fails, those credits come back. Add any AI label the platform asks for before you pay to run the ad.
Do not present the spokesperson as a real customer or a real review. Check TikTok and Meta rules before you spend more on ads. Say only what you can prove.
